page: Amazon Web Services m5.12xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine based on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. The instance is powered by dedicated Intel Xeon 8259CL x86_64 processors running at a base clock of 3.1 GHz. Compute capacity is split across 24 physical cores providing 48 vCPUs with hyper-threading enabled. Cache configuration includes 32 KB L1 data cache per core, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and a shared 35 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include support for AVX, AVX-512F, AES, BMI2, and FMA.

Memory capacity is configured with 192.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, maintaining a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include bundled local storage or dedicated hardware GPU accelerators. Network connectivity provides a baseline network throughput of 12 Gbps, while public IPv4 addresses are not included complimentary.

Benchmark results place the instance primarily in the middle 50% for multi-threaded and system throughput workloads, including a PassMark CPU score of 34,538.76, Geekbench multi-core score of 10,676.0, and stress-ng multi-core performance of 40,455.21. Memory bandwidth reaches 108.48 GB/sec for large un-cached reads and 47.89 GB/sec for un-cached writes. However, single-core processing capabilities fall into the lower 25% percentile, as reflected by a Geekbench single-core score of 1,157.0 and single-threaded gzip compression performance of 23.64 GB/sec.

Qualitatively, m5.12xlarge delivers predictable mid-range resource density across extensive core allocations, though modern workloads requiring maximum single-thread responsiveness or high-parameter AI model inference demonstrate clear performance tradeoffs. The hardware profile is suited for distributed multi-threaded environments, such as relational databases, enterprise web-serving fleets, CI/CD build farms, and memory-balanced data transformation pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services m5.12xlarge is a Nitro-based general-purpose instance featuring 48 dedicated vCPUs (24 physical cores) on Intel Xeon 8259CL processors clocked at 3.1 GHz, paired with 192.0 GB of DDR4 RAM at a balanced 1:4 core-to-memory ratio. It lacks local ephemeral storage and GPU acceleration, while provisioning a 12 Gbps baseline network capacity. Benchmark results indicate steady middle-tier multi-threaded compute, memory bandwidth, and caching metrics, alongside weaker single-core performance percentiles. With 108.48 GB/sec large-block read memory bandwidth and strong multi-core compilation results, this instance is suited for multi-threaded enterprise application stacks, backend web serving, build automation, and general relational database operations.
